One gating panel, drawn as GateLab draws it

Source: R/strategy_panel.R
gatelabPanelGrob.Rd

Draws a biaxial contour plot with its gates the way GateLab's Strategy and Illustration tabs do: density contours with the events outside the lowest contour as dots, d3's axes and ticks, the title above, each gate's outline with its name and share, and a quadrant gate as a crosshair with the four shares. Sizes are the app's, in CSS pixels (96 to the inch), so a panel is the same picture as in the app at any scale.

Usage

gatelabPanelGrob(
  x,
  y,
  xlim,
  ylim,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  gates = list(),
  plot_size = 300,
  contour_levels = 10L,
  contour_threshold = 5,
  bandwidth = NULL,
  point_alpha = 0.35,
  point_size = 1.2,
  pub_style = TRUE,
  gate_line_width = 1.5,
  label_background = 0.6,
  quadrant_labels = c("corner", "centre"),
  bold_labels = FALSE,
  font_sizes = c(tick = 12, axis = 12, title = 12, gate = 12),
  scale = 1,
  family = "",
  true_hyphen = TRUE
)

Arguments

x, y

The events to draw, in display units; see gatelabDisplayEvents.

xlim, ylim

The axis ranges, each c(low, high).

xlab, ylab

Axis titles.

title

The panel's title (the app writes the parent population and its count).

gates

The gates to draw: a list, each a list with type, name, color, and vertices (two-column matrix, display units), percent, label_offset and label_placed for an outlined gate, or center, quadrant_pcts (four values, in the order top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left) and quadrant_label_offsets for a quadrant gate. A gate_id is optional: it names the gate's entry in the anchors attribute.

plot_size

Side of the panel in pixels, margins included.

contour_levels, contour_threshold, bandwidth

Passed to gatelabContour.

point_alpha

Opacity of the outlier dots; the contour lines take 0.15 more.

point_size

Radius of the outlier dots in pixels (the app's "Point size").

pub_style

Publication style: black gates and labels. FALSE draws each gate in its own colour with a white label on a box of that colour.

gate_line_width

Gate line width in pixels.

label_background

Under publication style, opacity of the white backing behind a gate label and behind each quadrant's share, so they read over the events; 0 draws none.

quadrant_labels

Where a quadrant gate's four shares are written: "corner", in the corners of the plot as quadrant statistics usually are, or "centre", in the middle of each quadrant as the app places them. A share whose label was moved in the app is drawn where it was moved to.

bold_labels

Gate labels in bold.

font_sizes

Font sizes in pixels, named tick, axis, title and gate.

scale

Multiplies every size, for a larger or smaller panel of the same proportions.

family

Font family; "" takes the device's sans-serif face.

true_hyphen

R's pdf() and postscript() devices draw a hyphen as a minus sign, so a population named CD4- would end in a longer dash than in the app. TRUE draws the hyphen glyph on those devices in titles, axis titles and gate labels; tick labels keep the minus sign.

Value

A grid gTree of class gatelab_panel, plot_size * scale / 96 inches square. Its attribute anchors holds, by gate id, how far down the panel each gate's label sits (pixels), which is where a strategy's arrows leave from, and its attribute geometry the margins, ticks and axis-title offsets the panel was drawn with.

Details

Ported from GateLab's renderMiniPlot with the margin, label and quadrant rules GateLab applies to it. Contour mode only: the app's other plot modes are not drawn. A quadrant's shares are written in the corners of the plot unless quadrant_labels = "centre", which is where the app writes them.

The panel is a grid gTree of a fixed size. print() and plot() draw it on a new page of the current device; grid::grid.draw() adds it to the page as it is.

See also

gatelabStrategyPlot, which lays out one panel per gating step.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- c(rnorm(3000, 1, 0.5), rnorm(3000, 4, 0.6))
y <- c(rnorm(3000, 4, 0.6), rnorm(3000, 1, 0.5))
gate <- list(type = "polygon", gate_id = "g1", name = "CD4_positive", color = "#e41a1c",
             percent = 50, vertices = cbind(c(2.5, 6, 6, 2.5), c(-0.5, -0.5, 2.5, 2.5)))
panel <- gatelabPanelGrob(x, y, xlim = c(-1, 7), ylim = c(-1, 7), xlab = "CD4", ylab = "CD8",
                          title = "All Events (6,000)", gates = list(gate))
plot(panel)
